All 543 constituencies, fewest voters to most

How the number is worked out

Vote value = average electors per seat in India divided by electors in the seat. 1.00 is the national average. Above 1, fewer voters share the MP, so each vote counts for more. Below 1, more voters share the MP. Rank 1 is the seat where one vote counts most.

Sources: Election Commission of India, General Election 2024 statistical reports; constituency electors from the ECI phase-wise annexures published through PIB (phases 1 to 3, phase 4, phase 5, phase 6, phase 7). They exclude service electors. Surat is approximate (about 17.67 lakh, from a Deccan Herald report). Outer Manipur is the sum of its two polling phases. Map outlines: DataMeet.

Assam's seats were redrawn in 2023, so its shapes are the older outlines matched to the nearest new seat, and small seats such as Lakshadweep or the Delhi and Mumbai seats are hard to see at this size. Use the lists and the checker for those. This measures how many voters share one MP, not turnout or an MP's performance.
